title: YouTube as a source of information on gout: a quality analysis
screen_reason: Cross-sectional analysis of 114 English-language YouTube videos retrieved with four gout keywords. Beyond the DISCERN and GQS rating scales, every video was given an explicit usefulness verdict by two blinded rheumatologists — 'useful' if it contained scientifically accurate information, 'misleading' if it contained at least one scientifically unproven statement — and the share of the sample coded misleading is reported with its denominator (14/114 = 12.28%). Explicit misleading coding against expert verification is CONTENT under §3, so the paper is not quality-only despite its title.

estimates.country: Not stated; English-language YouTube search (authors based in Turkey)
estimates.date: Search conducted 1 December 2020; videos uploaded between 21 October 2010 and 2020 (median 916.5 days on YouTube)
estimates.measure_type: % of gout-related YouTube videos coded as containing misleading information
estimates.denominator: 114 English-language gout videos meeting inclusion criteria, from the top 60 relevance-ranked results for each of four search terms (240 screened; 95 duplicates, 13 non-English, 9 irrelevant, 8 music videos and 1 without audio excluded)
estimates.definition: A video was coded misleading if it included at least one piece of scientifically unproven information; useful if it included scientifically accurate information about any aspect of the disease (symptoms, clinical features, diagnosis, treatment, prevention). The two categories are mutually exclusive and exhaust the sample.
estimates.misinfo_def: No formal definition of misinformation; operationalised as content that is not scientifically accurate: "the videos were considered as useful if they included scientifically accurate information about any aspect of the disease (e.g., symptoms, clinical features, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention) or misleading if they included at least one scientifically unproven information"

estimates.page_loc: p. 1323, Results, 'Video usefulness'; counts repeated in Table 3 (Detailed characteristics of YouTube videos according to their usefulness) and in the Abstract
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two rheumatologists (M.E.O. and O.Z.) assessed all 114 videos blindly; discrepancies resolved by reassessment and consensus. Cohen's kappa for inter-observer agreement was 0.925 (95% CI 0.883-1.000). The usefulness criterion follows prior YouTube studies; no external fact-check list or written codebook is reproduced.
estimates.moderator_quote: Therefore, we sampled the top 60 videos
estimates.notes: denom_selection=curated because the frame is the top 60 relevance-ranked results per search term under YouTube's default sort, explicitly chosen on the ground that most users do not look past the first three pages. Single-disease keyword corpus, so denom_scope=topical. Construct call worth an adjudicator's eye: the numerator criterion is 'at least one scientifically unproven information', which is broader than false — an accurate video containing one unsupported claim qualifies, and 'unproven' is not the same as 'wrong'. It still sits on the CONTENT side of §3 because it is an explicit accurate/misleading verdict against expert clinical judgement rather than a coverage or presentation score, and because a wholly accurate video cannot receive the label. breadth is coded misleading to reflect the loose threshold. Note also that misleading videos had significantly higher viewership (median 67,134 vs 15,555 views), so an exposure-weighted share would be considerably higher than 12.28%; the paper does not compute one.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted: (1) the GQS quality bands (high 57.89%, intermediate 28.95%, low 13.16% of 114 videos) — a Global Quality Scale rating with no truth judgement, so construct QUALITY under §3, left out because the paper already yields a direct CONTENT estimate; an adjudicator who records QUALITY rows wherever they appear can add 'GQS low = 13.16% of 114'. (2) The misleading share by video source (independent users 4/7 = 57.14%, healthcare professionals other than physicians 3/10 = 30%, health information websites 5/35 = 14.29%, physicians 2/42 = 4.76%, academic institutions/professional organizations 0/20 = 0%) and by target audience (patients 13/81 = 16.05%, healthcare professionals 1/26 = 3.85%) — source and audience subgroups of the same sample rather than the paper's headline; the independent-user figure rests on 7 videos. (3) Topic composition of the 114 videos (gout diet 28.07%, treatment 21.05%, acute attack 21.05%, overview 14.04%, comorbidities 7.02%, pathophysiology 4.39%, surgery 4.39%) — subject matter, not veracity. (4) Source composition (physicians 36.84%, health information websites 30.70%, academic institutions 17.54%, other health professionals 8.77%, independent users 6.14%). (5) Median DISCERN (3.0) and GQS (4.0) scores, all view/like/dislike/comment medians and the Mann-Whitney and Kruskal-Wallis results — no share with a misinformation denominator. (6) Useful-video rates quoted from other diseases (Sjogren's 51.4%, rheumatoid arthritis 54.9%, spondyloarthritis 86%, SLE 83.60%) and the '80% of internet users access health information online' figure are all cited from other papers, excluded under R8.

rob.design: Cross-sectional observational content analysis of YouTube, searched 1 December 2020 with the keywords 'gout', 'gout arthritis', 'gout treatment' and 'gout diet' under the default relevance filter; top 60 videos per term sampled (240 total), English only, duplicates, irrelevant, music and audio-free videos excluded, leaving 114. No response rate applies. Two rheumatologists assessed all videos blindly with discrepancies resolved by consensus; Cohen's kappa 0.925 (95% CI 0.883-1.000). Reliability and quality also scored with a modified five-point DISCERN and the five-point Global Quality Scale. Weaknesses: relevance-ranked top-N frame that changes over time, English only, no pre-registered codebook for the useful/misleading judgement, and no separate reliability figure for the usefulness coding as distinct from the scales.
